newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine may limit foreign T-bill buying -C.bank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine may limit foreign T-bill buying -C.bank.

text.p: Ukraine is considering limiting participation by non-residents on the Treasury-bill market, a top central bank official said on Tuesday.
"At this time, the Finance Ministry is gently telling non-residents that its chief plans are aimed at Ukrainian residents," said the official, who asked not to be named.
"Participation by non-residents on the Treasury-bill market already accounts for up to 80 percent of such transactions."
He did not say when restrictions might be in place on the T-bill market, where the nominal value of all paper issued in 1996 was more than 3.7 billion hryvnia ($1.96 million).
The official and dealers said foreigners were generally buying longer-term nine-month and 12-month T-bills but said they practically never purchased three-month paper.
Ukraine's T-bills are also issued in six-month maturities.
Dealers said foreigners usually purchase no less than $5 million (nine million hryvnias) in a paper at a time.
The ministry on Tuesday limited issue volumes for the first time to five million hryvnias for nine- and 12-month issues, following limits on nine-months which began earlier this month.
"Ukrainian banks still do not have a lot of money, and this has caused a historical scare in the area of any long-term investments," the official said.
Dealers said the largest foreign buyers of Ukrainian T-bills include CS First Boston, Societe Generale and Credit Lyonnais.
Ukrainian T-bills are auctioned, usually twice weekly, by the central bank, and are traded eletronically on the interbank market.
Ukrainian dealers also said Latvian, Lithuanian, Cypriot and Czech banks were also big buyers. Those countries have the right to take T-bill income out of Ukraine duty-free.
Bank Ukraina dealer Olexander Okhrymenko said non-residents were earning about 17 percent in annualised interest on nine-month paper and 22 percent annualised interest on 12-month bills.
One foreign bank official said it was difficult to predict future T-bill yields until Ukraine passes its federal budget, which will set the amount of paper the government will issue.
